WHY A SECOND BUDGET RATHER THAN A REVISION. `con:loop-status-warm-latency-ms` limits the WARM case (no write since the last call) to 2,000 ms and is currently MET: 1,291 ms measured 2026-09-12. But `fact:loop-status-cost-is-amplifiers-not-baseline-and-80pc-of-calls-are-automation` shows the warm case is not the case anyone waits on — the same call is 4,096 ms steady once a write precedes each one, because the derived-scan memo is keyed per write generation and a session that is WORKING invalidates it every time. A budget that only measures the state a session is rarely in cannot fail when the thing gets slow, which is the whole job of a budget.

THE NUMBER IS ANTHONY'S RULING, 2026-09-12, and the tighter derivation is recorded here so it can be argued rather than rediscovered. He asked for "seconds to under 1s" as the goal across the tool surface and chose 1,000 ms for this one. A STRICTER DERIVATION EXISTS AND GIVES 332 ms: loop_nudge fires this check on PostToolUse of every reflow2 call, so it is an INSTRUMENT ATTACHED TO OTHER WORK, and an instrument should not cost more than about twice the work it observes. Measured over the same ledger, the median reflow2 write is 166 ms (n=76; 154 ms over all 115 non-loop_status calls), so 2x the work it follows is 332 ms. 1,000 ms is therefore a CEILING, at 6x the median write it trails — deliberately loose, and the tighter number is the one to reach for if the levers turn out to allow it.

MEASURED BEFORE THE BUDGET WAS WRITTEN, 2026-09-12, reflow2-mcp 0.59.0 release, on a physical copy of the live store (4,343 nodes / 25,004 edges), shared transport with --export-to, load 0.1-0.4, medians of 4:
  no write before the call   1,291 ms   (under the old warm budget)
  one write before each call 4,096 ms   <- THIS BUDGET'S QUANTITY, 4.1x over
And in production that day the median observed was 12,089 ms, because concurrency (x1.6 at four clients) and machine load (up to x6 under a cargo build) stack on top.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so it is not quoted as a portable guarantee: one machine (4 cores), release build, this store at this size, stdio and shared transports, an uncontended box. It says nothing about cold start, nothing about the other rollups, and nothing about what the same call costs on a design ten times this size. It is also NOT a claim that 1,000 ms is achievable — the baseline alone is 1,284 ms warm, so meeting this budget REQUIRES attacking the intrinsic scan cost that was left unstarted on 2026-09-05, not only the write tax."}
